newsitem.title: UK: Iraq oil on spot market for first time in six years.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil on spot market for first time in six years.

text.p: Iraqi crude oil emerged on the international spot market for the first time in six years after Baghdad began oil sales under a U.N. oil-for-food exchange three weeks ago, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders said a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) of Iraqi Kirkuk crude was being offered into Rotterdam by Taurus, a Swiss-based trading house.
"We've had firm indications from Taurus," said a London-based crude trader.
Taurus was said by traders to be handling crude under contract to Russia's Lukoil.
Taurus declined comment. Lukoil was not immediately available for comment.
Lukoil has a 17,000 barrel a day (bpd) contract with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) under the United Nations $2 billion Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
A spot sale of Kirkuk would be the first on the international market since U.N. sanctions were slapped on Iraq for its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
The Kirkuk cargo, of some two million barrels, is scheduled to load from Iraq's Turkish pipeline outlet at Ceyhan on the Mediterranean on Wednesday.
Dealers said initial offers for the crude were at benchmark Dated Brent less 60 cents cif Rotterdam.
The crude is valued at roughly the same price, on a delivered basis, as Russia's Urals blend crude.
Urals on Tuesday was valued at Dated Brent less 70-75 cents cif NWE and at Dated Brent less $1.10 cif Med.
Traders said they were expecting a second spot cargo, of Kirkuk to be offered on the spot market soon.
Russia's Nafta Moscow is expected to put its mid-January shipment from Ceyhan on sale to European refiners.

Most of the 500,000 bpd of Iraqi crude sales required to meet an initial $2 billion target over a six month period are committed to companies with their own refining facilities and will not appear for sale on spot markets.
